1.title: Data Security Controls
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Data Security Controls. This module covers task statement one point three, the last task of Domain one. You will learn how to encrypt data at rest and in transit, write access policies for data and keys, back up and retain data, find sensitive data, and prove compliance. The exam describes a data requirement and asks you to choose the control that fits.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Encrypt data at rest with A W S K M S, and in transit with A C M and T L S. Write access policies for data and for encryption keys, and rotate keys and renew certificates. Implement backups, replication, retention and lifecycle policies. Classify data and align services to compliance needs. And choose between look-alike services, such as K M S and CloudHSM.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom Protects the Ledger
1.text: Lantern and Loom now holds customer addresses, invoices and an order database. An auditor asks three questions: is it encrypted, who can read it, and can anyone delete it? A teammate has also deleted a bucket's contents by mistake, and invoices must be kept for seven years. Your job is to choose the data controls, from keys to backups.

1.title: The Data Protection Cycle
1.text: Data protection runs in six steps. Classify: find sensitive data with Macie. Encrypt: at rest with K M S, and in transit with T L S and A C M. Control access: with policies, Block Public Access and key policies. Back up and replicate: with A W S Backup, snapshots and S three replication. Retain and expire: with Object Lock and lifecycle rules. And audit: with CloudTrail, Config and Artifact. The figure shows the six steps in order. Exam tip: name the data need first: classify, encrypt, restrict, recover, retain or audit.

1.title: AWS KMS Key Types
1.text: A W S K M S has three kinds of key. An A W S owned key is managed by the A W S service and is hidden from you. It is free, and the service decides the rotation. An A W S managed key has an alias that starts with a W S slash and the service name. K M S manages it for you, you can view it, and it rotates automatically every year. There is no monthly fee, only a per-use fee. A customer managed key is yours: you control the policy, the rotation and the deletion. Rotation is optional, and there is a monthly fee plus a per-use fee. K M S keys are Regional, and resources under an A W S managed key cannot be shared with other accounts. Exam tip: control, audit or cross-account sharing means a customer managed key.

1.title: Envelope Encryption and Key Policies
1.text: K M S uses envelope encryption. K M S generates a data key. The data key encrypts your data. The K M S key encrypts the data key. Both ciphertexts are stored together, and to read the data, K M S decrypts the data key first. The figure shows this. Access to a K M S key is controlled mainly by its key policy. The default key policy lets the account use I A M policies to grant access. To use a key from another account, you need permission in the key policy and an I A M policy in the other account. Grants let A W S services use a key on your behalf, and every use is logged in CloudTrail. Exam tip: a K M S key works only if its key policy allows it, directly or through I A M.

1.title: Key Rotation and Multi-Region Keys
1.text: Now rotation. Customer managed symmetric keys have optional automatic rotation, every three hundred sixty-five days by default, or a custom period, and you can also rotate on demand. A W S managed keys rotate automatically every year, and you cannot change that. Rotation changes the key material, not the key I D or A R N, and old material is kept, so older data still decrypts. Rotation does not re-encrypt your data. Asymmetric keys, H M A C keys and custom key store keys are rotated manually, with a new key and an alias. Multi-Region keys are related keys in several Regions, and rotation is set on the primary key. Exam tip: rotation is transparent, with no code change and no re-encryption.

1.title: AWS KMS or AWS CloudHSM?
1.text: K M S or CloudHSM? K M S is a managed key service, where A W S runs the hardware, and you control access with I A M and key policies. It integrates with many services. CloudHSM gives you your own hardware security modules in the cloud. They are single-tenant and general purpose. You manage the keys and users, outside I A M, and A W S cannot see the key material. In Fips mode, the modules are validated at Fips one forty level three. K M S is the default choice. Choose CloudHSM when you need dedicated H S M s or your own algorithms. Exam tip: dedicated single-tenant H S M s and full control mean CloudHSM; everything else, K M S.

1.title: Encrypting Data at Rest
1.text: Three services come up most. In S three, every new object is encrypted by default with S S E dash S three. Choose S S E dash K M S or D S S E dash K M S when you need key control and audit. Changing the default does not re-encrypt old objects. In E B S, you encrypt with a K M S key, there is an encryption by default account setting, and snapshots of encrypted volumes stay encrypted. To encrypt an unencrypted volume, snapshot it and copy the snapshot encrypted. In R D S, you choose encryption at creation. It covers storage, logs, backups and replicas, and it cannot be turned off. To encrypt an existing database, restore from an encrypted snapshot copy. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, S three now disables S S E dash C by default on new buckets, so check the page. Exam tip: to encrypt an existing unencrypted volume or database, copy a snapshot with encryption on.

1.title: Encrypting Data in Transit with ACM
1.text: T L S encrypts data between clients and services. A W S Certificate Manager, or A C M, creates, stores and renews public and private certificates, with no extra charge for the certificates it manages. Certificates attach to load balancers, CloudFront and A P I Gateway. They are Regional, and CloudFront needs its certificate in the U S East, Northern Virginia, Region. An S three bucket policy can deny requests that do not use H T T P S, and can set a minimum T L S version. A W S also encrypts traffic between Regions and between Availability Zones on its own network. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, A C M can also issue certificates for other servers through Acme, so check the page. Exam tip: a public H T T P S certificate for a load balancer or CloudFront means A C M.

1.title: Keeping S3 Data Private
1.text: S three Block Public Access has four settings: block public A C L s, ignore public A C L s, block public policies, and restrict public buckets. You can apply it at the organization, account, bucket or access point level. It overrides policies and A C L s, and the most restrictive setting wins. New buckets do not allow public access by default. Object Ownership set to bucket owner enforced, which is the default, disables A C L s, so policies control access. I A M Access Analyzer for S three reviews public and shared buckets. Exam tip: keep everything private by default; turn on all four settings at the account level.

1.title: Access Policies for Data
1.text: Bucket policies use conditions to enforce rules. To allow only your organization, use a bucket policy with the aws principal org I D condition. To allow only your V P C, use the source V P C endpoint or source V P C condition, plus a V P C endpoint policy. For H T T P S only, deny requests when secure transport is false. To require encrypted uploads, add a condition on the server-side encryption header. To use a key from another account, you need a key policy and an I A M policy. A deny with a condition enforces a rule on every request. Exam tip: an explicit deny with a condition is how you enforce a data rule everywhere.

2.title: Retention and Recovery in S3
2.text: For retention and recovery in S three, start with Versioning, which keeps every version, so an overwrite or a delete can be undone. Object Lock is write once, read many, and it needs versioning. Compliance mode blocks every user, including root. Governance mode lets specially permitted users override it. A legal hold has no expiry; it stays until you remove it. Replication copies objects to another bucket: cross-Region replication, or C R R, to another Region, and same-Region replication, or S R R, in the same Region. Live replication copies new objects only; use Batch Replication for existing ones. Replication Time Control targets fifteen minutes. Exam tip: cannot be deleted by anyone, even root, means Object Lock in compliance mode.

2.title: Backups with AWS Backup
2.text: A W S Backup centralizes backups. A backup plan sets the schedule, the retention and the lifecycle to cold storage, and you can assign resources by tag. Backups are stored in backup vaults, and Vault Lock gives write once, read many protection against deletion. You can copy backups across Regions and across accounts, and Organizations policies apply plans to every account. Audit Manager reports show compliance. It covers E B S, R D S, Aurora, DynamoDB, E F S, F S x, S three and more. The figure shows one plan writing to a locked vault and copying to another Region and another account. Exam tip: central, scheduled, cross-Region and tamper-proof backups mean A W S Backup with Vault Lock.

2.title: Discovering Sensitive Data with Amazon Macie
2.text: Amazon Macie finds sensitive data in S three, using machine learning and pattern matching. Managed data identifiers cover personal, financial and credentials data, and custom data identifiers use your own patterns. Macie also reviews bucket security: public, unencrypted or shared buckets raise policy findings. You can run automated discovery, or discovery jobs, once or on a schedule. Findings flow to EventBridge and Security Hub, and Organizations manages many accounts. Exam tip: to find personal data in S three buckets, use Macie.

2.title: Auditing and Compliance: CloudTrail, Config and Artifact
2.text: Three services help you prove compliance. A W S CloudTrail answers: who did what, and when? It keeps ninety days of event history, trails deliver events to S three, and CloudTrail Lake handles long retention. A W S Config answers: how was it configured, and is it compliant? It keeps configuration history, evaluates rules and conformance packs, uses aggregators for many accounts, and can remediate. A W S Artifact answers: what does A W S attest? It gives on-demand reports, such as S O C, short for System and Organization Controls,, I S O, short for International Organization for Standardization, and P C I, plus agreements, free of charge. Exam tip: activity is CloudTrail, configuration is Config, and A W S's own reports are Artifact.

2.title: Data Lifecycle Policies
2.text: Lifecycle policies manage data over time. S three Lifecycle transitions objects to cheaper classes and expires them. Rules apply to existing and new objects, and can filter by prefix, tags or size. A bucket policy cannot stop a lifecycle rule from running. A W S Backup has its own lifecycle: it moves backups to cold storage, and deletes them after the retention period. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager automates E B S snapshots and A M I s: creation, retention and deletion, at no extra cost. Keep data as long as the rules require, and no longer. Exam tip: archive then delete on a schedule means lifecycle rules; scheduled E B S snapshots mean Data Lifecycle Manager.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Data Security
2.text: Here is what the exam asks about data security. Which key: A W S owned, A W S managed, customer managed, K M S or CloudHSM. Which encryption step: at rest, in transit, rotation or certificate renewal. Which access control: Block Public Access, a bucket policy condition or a key policy. Which recovery or retention tool: versioning, Object Lock, replication, Backup or lifecycle. And which audit or discovery service: Macie, CloudTrail, Config or Artifact. Exam tip: look for the verbs: encrypt, restrict, recover, retain, discover or prove.

2.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom Protects the Ledger
2.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Auditors must see key use, and the team controls the policy: S S E dash K M S with a customer managed key. The order database is unencrypted: an encrypted copy of a snapshot, then restore. H T T P S for the site on CloudFront: an A C M certificate in U S East, Northern Virginia. Only our organization may read a bucket: a bucket policy with the principal org I D condition, and Block Public Access. Invoices kept seven years and never deleted: Object Lock in compliance mode. A mistaken delete must be reversible: S three Versioning. Central backups with copies elsewhere: A W S Backup with cross-Region copy and Vault Lock. Which buckets hold personal data: Macie. And an auditor wants A W S's I S O report: A W S Artifact.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. For keys, choose customer managed keys for control, remember that rotation is transparent, and use CloudHSM for dedicated H S M s. For encryption, S S E dash S three is the default, S S E dash K M S gives audit, and A C M provides T L S certificates. For access, use Block Public Access, bucket policy conditions and key policies. For retention and recovery, use Versioning, Object Lock, replication, A W S Backup and lifecycle rules. And to prove it, use Macie, CloudTrail, Config and Artifact.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Lantern and Loom needs full control of a K M S key's policy, rotation and deletion, and wants to share encrypted E B S snapshots with a partner account. Which type of key should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: a customer managed K M S key. It gives full control and can be shared through its key policy. A W S owned keys are hidden, resources under A W S managed keys cannot be shared with other accounts, and CloudHSM is for dedicated H S M s.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Order exports in Amazon S three must be encrypted with a key whose use auditors can follow in CloudTrail, and the team must control the key policy. What should the architect configure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: S S E dash K M S with a customer managed key. It logs every key use in CloudTrail and lets the team control the key policy. S S E dash S three and the default give no key-level audit, and S S E dash C leaves key handling to the application.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. Which two statements about A W S K M S key rotation are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are B and D. Automatic rotation is optional on customer managed symmetric keys, and K M S keeps old key material, so older data still decrypts. The key I D does not change, existing data is not re-encrypted, and A W S managed keys rotate every year automatically.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Lantern and Loom's order database runs on an unencrypted Amazon R D S instance. Compliance now requires encryption at rest. What is the correct approach? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: snapshot the instance, copy the snapshot with encryption, and restore from the copy. An R D S instance can be encrypted only at creation, so the encrypted snapshot copy is how you add encryption.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Lantern and Loom must keep invoice files for seven years so that no one, including the root user, can delete or overwrite them. Which design meets this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: S three Object Lock in compliance mode, with versioning and a seven-year retention period. Compliance mode blocks every user, including root. Governance mode can be bypassed, a bucket policy can be changed, and a lifecycle rule only deletes.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. Lantern and Loom wants central, scheduled backups of E B S volumes, R D S databases and DynamoDB tables, with copies in a second Region and protection against anyone deleting the backups. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A W S Backup with a plan, cross-Region copy and Vault Lock. Manual snapshots are not central, and replication and Config do not back up these services.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. The security team must find out which S three buckets contain personal data such as names and card numbers, and whether any of those buckets are public. Which service should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Amazon Macie. It discovers sensitive data with machine learning and pattern matching, and evaluates bucket security. GuardDuty detects threats, Config records configuration, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. Lantern and Loom serves its site through Amazon CloudFront on its own domain over H T T P S. It wants a certificate that renews automatically at no extra certificate cost. Where should it request the certificate? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: in A W S Certificate Manager in the U S East, Northern Virginia, Region. A certificate used with CloudFront must be requested there. K M S and CloudHSM manage keys, not renewing website certificates.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all eight answers. Question one: C. Question two: B. Question three: B and D. Question four: D. Question five: A. Question six: C. Question seven: B. Question eight: A. That completes Domain one. In Module four, we start Domain two: scalable and loosely coupled architectures.
